transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because I just feel like I can't settle inside my own skin anymore. It's like... I always have this urge to jump up and start doing the next thing, even when I'm completely worn out and really just need to be sitting still. It's exhausting.
Are these uncomfortable sensations or the urge to move mostly felt in your legs, or throughout your entire body?

I wouldn't say it's just in my legs. It's more... well, it's really my whole body. I just get this overall feeling everywhere that I need to get up and do something. I haven't noticed it being focused in my legs at all.

```json
{"intent": "Determine if the physical restlessness and need to be on the go has been present since childhood to evaluate for ADHD", "question": "Did you experience this same urge

Yes, it's been like this for as long as I can remember. Even back in grade school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but careless. I was always losing my papers, or talking out of turn. They were constantly having to give me reminders just to stay in my seat or to actually finish my work. So, yes, it's definitely been there since I was young.
Do you often find yourself overwhelmed by persistent and uncontrollable worries about everyday life events or responsibilities?

No, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier like that. I mean, I get stressed sometimes like anyone else, but I don't sit around feeling overwhelmed by constant worrying about everyday things. My problem is more just... not being able to focus or sit still, rather than being anxious about everything.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether the patient currently meets criteria for inattentive symptoms such as distractibility or difficulty sustaining focus in daily life", "question": "In your day

In my day-to-day life, I have a terrible time staying focused. Like, if I'm sitting at the kitchen table trying to sort through the bills or handle paperwork... it just takes nothing to pull me away. A car door slamming outside, my phone screen lighting up, or even just suddenly thinking about what I need to do in the garden. Once that happens, I'm completely off track and I forget what I was even trying to do in the first place.
